unit: One selected care-item/indication row; not patients, unique procedures or national coverage rates
rule: Classify the service and indication, not the drug name or assumed patient identity. Keep anatomy, reproductive physiology, sex-defined eligibility and disease burden distinct. Mixed or underspecified rows require component-level extraction.

groups.label: Shared body systems / functions
groups.definition: Anatomy or function present in both sexes; eligibility and burden may still differ.
groups.approach: Compare women and men with comparable clinical need, including unmet care, within the same condition and service. Assess clinical eligibility independently of reimbursement rules.

groups.label: Female reproductive anatomy
groups.definition: The recorded service directly targets a specified female reproductive organ or tissue.
groups.approach: Assess organ-specific clinical need and benefit. Compare other services only when purpose, complexity and resources are defensibly comparable.

groups.label: Male reproductive anatomy
groups.definition: The recorded service directly targets a specified male reproductive organ or function.
groups.approach: Assess organ-specific clinical need and benefit. Compare other services only when purpose, complexity and resources are defensibly comparable.

groups.label: Female reproductive physiology
groups.definition: The indication concerns menopause, ovulation or related reproductive physiology, including systemic treatment.
groups.approach: Compare access among clinically eligible patients and alternative treatments. Analyze reproductive physiology separately from organ-specific procedures.

groups.label: Male reproductive physiology
groups.definition: The recorded indication concerns male reproductive endocrine function; the hormone itself is not exclusive to men.
groups.approach: Compare access for documented indications, accounting for diagnostic thresholds, benefit, alternatives, monitoring and treatment risks.

groups.label: Mixed or site-dependent
groups.definition: A bundled row includes distinct anatomical components, adapted techniques or an unresolved treatment site.
groups.approach: Separate diagnosis, organ/site and procedure components before estimating sex comparisons. Do not assign the entire row to one sex.

sources.title: Male Breast Cancer
sources.role: Clinical classification guidance; breast tissue is present in both sexes.

sources.organization: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
sources.title: About Endometriosis
sources.role: Clinical classification guidance; endometriosis can involve reproductive and other anatomical sites.

sources.organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.title: Treatments for Bladder Control Problems (Urinary Incontinence)
sources.role: Clinical classification guidance; pelvic-floor therapy can apply to women and men.

sources.organization: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases
sources.title: Osteoporosis in Men
sources.role: Clinical classification guidance; osteoporosis is not limited to women.

items.sex_feature: Menopause indication; systemic hormone treatment
items.notes: Classified by menopausal indication, not estradiol as a molecule. Other indications require separate rows.

items.sex_feature: Menopause indication; systemic hormone treatment
items.notes: Route and formulary restrictions remain separate from the physiology classification.

items.sex_feature: Vaginal tissue; menopausal indication
items.notes: Local vaginal treatment is distinguished from systemic treatment of menopausal vasomotor symptoms.

items.sex_feature: Menopause plus a uterine/endometrial requirement
items.notes: Primary purpose is systemic menopausal treatment; progestogen provides endometrial protection. Preserve the uterus requirement as an additional anatomical feature.

items.sex_feature: Menopausal vasomotor indication
items.notes: Nonhormonal mechanism does not make the menopausal indication a general shared condition.

items.sex_feature: Menopausal vasomotor indication
items.notes: Classify this dose and indication separately from paroxetine used for other conditions.

items.sex_feature: Vulvovaginal tissue; menopausal indication
items.notes: Oral administration does not change the anatomical target of this recorded indication.

items.sex_feature: Vaginal tissue; menopausal indication
items.notes: Local treatment of menopausal vulvovaginal symptoms; do not classify all uses of the molecule together.

items.sex_feature: Penile erectile function
items.notes: This row concerns erectile dysfunction. Sildenafil for pulmonary vascular disease would need a separate shared-system row and coverage assessment.

items.sex_feature: Sexual desire is shared; recorded drug indication is for women
items.approach: Assess access for women meeting the clinical indication, alternatives and consistency of sexual-health benefit rules. Do not require an off-label male comparator.
items.notes: A women-specific labeled population is not an exclusive anatomical structure. Preserve formulation and label-year limits.

items.sex_feature: Sexual desire is shared; recorded drug indication is for women
items.approach: Assess access for women meeting the clinical indication, alternatives and consistency of sexual-health benefit rules. Do not require an off-label male comparator.
items.notes: Separate sex-defined drug eligibility from anatomy, clinical benefit and the sexual-dysfunction benefit exclusion.

items.sex_feature: Documented male hypogonadism indication
items.notes: Testosterone and endocrine pathways are not exclusive to men. Classification applies only to this recorded indication.

items.sex_feature: Shared incontinence indication; male/female surgical components
items.notes: Sex-adapted sling procedures are bundled. Compare their individual codes and clinical resources; a shared symptom does not make operations identical.

items.sex_feature: Shared incontinence pathway; male/female surgical components
items.notes: Separate sling revision/removal codes, technique and complexity before comparing payment.

items.sex_feature: Breast anatomy is shared; indication is postmastectomy reconstruction
items.notes: Do not equate a predominantly female literature sample with exclusively female anatomy.

items.sex_feature: Breast anatomy is shared; postmastectomy indication
items.notes: Record the population actually studied and the benefit rule separately from organ classification.

items.sex_feature: Breast anatomy is shared; cosmetic indication
items.notes: The distinction from medically necessary reconstruction is purpose and benefit eligibility, not sex alone.

items.sex_feature: Shared breast tissue; gynecomastia indication concerns men
items.notes: A male-associated diagnosis does not make breast tissue male-exclusive.

items.sex_feature: Shared breast tissue; symptom-defined indication
items.notes: Preserve symptom burden, clinical indication and actual patient population rather than assuming a women-only service.

items.sex_feature: Pelvic-floor and continence function in both sexes
items.notes: Compare eligibility and response within matched indications; exercises may be adapted to anatomy.

items.sex_feature: Pelvic-floor and continence function in both sexes
items.notes: Home versus clinician-delivered treatment is a benefit-setting distinction.

items.sex_feature: Shared bladder and neural function
items.notes: Underlying disease and eligible symptoms, rather than sex alone, define the comparison.

items.sex_feature: Pelvic-floor and continence function in both sexes
items.notes: Preserve the device and modality distinction from implanted nerve stimulation.

items.sex_feature: Shared pelvic pain plus vulvar-specific diagnoses
items.notes: This umbrella combines vulvodynia and other pelvic dysfunction. Extract diagnosis-specific eligibility and outcomes before assigning a single anatomy group.

items.sex_feature: Endometriosis; operative anatomy depends on lesion site
items.notes: Reproductive-tissue-related disease can affect bowel, bladder and other sites. Specify the operation and site; do not assume all surgery is confined to a reproductive organ.

items.sex_feature: Pelvic-organ prolapse; exact repair anatomy unresolved
items.notes: Provisional classification pending organ/site and procedure codes. Confirmed vaginal or uterine-support repairs can be classified as female reproductive anatomy.

items.sex_feature: Shared bone anatomy; women-specific estrogen-deficiency pathway
items.notes: A sex-specific eligibility route is a policy feature, not an anatomical restriction. Retain it when comparing with G05.

items.sex_feature: Shared bone anatomy; additional qualifying risk groups
items.notes: Compare testing access among clinically eligible beneficiaries, not unadjusted counts alone.

items.sex_feature: Shared breast tissue; recorded screening policy concerns women
items.notes: Keep screening eligibility distinct from diagnostic imaging and from the existence of breast tissue in men.

items.sex_feature: Prostate-dependent screening
items.notes: PSA and digital rectal screening differ in method and cost sharing; no female prostate-screening counterpart is required.

items.sex_feature: Uterine device placement for pregnancy prevention
items.notes: Separate anatomical suitability from the preventive versus therapeutic indication.

items.sex_feature: Cervix/vagina and screening indication
items.notes: Record organ presence, age and risk; a patient sex label alone does not establish clinical eligibility.

items.sex_feature: Uterus/endometrium; treatment indication
items.notes: Compare with the same device used for pregnancy prevention only after distinguishing medical purpose.

items.sex_feature: Male- and female-factor infertility components
items.notes: Separate cause, diagnostic service and treatment before cross-sex comparison.

items.sex_feature: Sperm, oocyte and embryo-related components
items.notes: Do not combine gamete collection, assisted reproduction and storage into an assumed identical service.

items.sex_feature: Vasectomy and tubal sterilization components
items.notes: A shared preventive purpose does not establish identical operative work or resources.

items.sex_feature: Ovulation/pregnancy prevention or menstrual treatment
items.notes: Separate each product and preventive or therapeutic indication; physiology and benefit purpose are distinct.

items.sex_feature: Fertility treatment can involve different reproductive functions
items.notes: Identify the drug and male- or female-factor indication before anatomy-specific synthesis.

items.sex_feature: Shared lymphatic system; includes breast-cancer sequelae
items.notes: A breast-cancer-survivor sample does not make lymphedema a female-exclusive condition. Preserve etiology and patient population.

items.sex_feature: Shared lymphatic system
items.notes: Compare access by indication, clinical severity and device requirements; analyze sex-related burden separately.
